summary: Instagram is carrying the channel: almost every video gets 1,000+ views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly gets under 60 views. The best performers are short 'X doesn't do Y, it only does Z' explainers about robots and sound-based gadgets (gyro robot, clap switch, mic). Videos on smoke alarms, taps, lift doors and the ultrasonic sensor, and any that were never posted to Instagram, get far fewer views and almost no shares or saves.
winningPattern: Hindi explainers on hands-on maker subjects (robots, clap switch, mic, DHT11) with a surprising 'it doesn't do X, it only does Y' or 'without this it fails' hook. Titles are short, use Hinglish, have one emoji, and are posted to Instagram first and YouTube second. Clap switch and robot topics also get real traction on YouTube (500-680 views), while generic 'how does X know?' questions do not.
doMore: Make more robot and clap-switch style videos: relatable builds with a visible 'failure' or surprise
Open with a bold contradiction such as 'X nahi, sirf Y' in the first line
Post every video to Instagram as well, since the unposted ones get zero there
Make follow-ups to winners (clap switch with a whistle, gyro robot falling) as a series
Add a clear share or save prompt, such as 'save this for your project', to build on the shares from the IR robot video
stopDoing: Generic 'Kaise Pata Chalta Hai? 🤔' titles on everyday objects like taps, lifts, malls and street lights
Posting near-duplicate topics (several smoke, IR and tap videos) that split views
Skipping Instagram or posting English-only videos, which have not worked here
